title.zh: 卷72 列傳第37 孝義
title.raw: 卷72 列傳第37 孝義 Volume 72 Biographies 37: Filial Piety

sentences.zh: 隋書卷七十二列傳第三十七

translations.literal: Book of Sui, Volume 72, Biographies 37
translations.idiomatic: Book of Sui, Volume 72, Biographies 37

sentences.zh: ○孝義

translations.literal: ○ Filial Piety and Righteous Conduct
translations.idiomatic: Filial Piety and Righteous Conduct

sentences.zh: 《孝經》云：「夫孝，天之經也，地之義也，人之行也。

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety says: "Filial piety is the constant of Heaven, the righteousness of Earth, and the conduct of man."
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety says: "Filial piety is Heaven's constant law, Earth's rightful duty, and the proper way of human conduct."

sentences.zh: 」《論語》云：「君子務本，本立而道生。

translations.literal: " The Analects says: "The gentleman devotes himself to the root; when the root is established, the Way comes forth."
translations.idiomatic: The Analects says: "The gentleman devotes himself to the root; once the root is firmly set, the Way arises from it."

sentences.zh: 孝悌也者，其為仁之本與！

translations.literal: Filial piety and brotherly respect — are these not the root of benevolence!"
translations.idiomatic: Are not filial piety and brotherly respect the very root of benevolence!"

sentences.zh: 」《呂覽》云：「夫孝，三皇、五帝之本務，萬事之綱紀也。

translations.literal: " The Lüshi Chunqiu says: "Filial piety is the fundamental task of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, the guiding principle of all affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The Lüshi Chunqiu says: "Filial piety was the essential duty of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, the governing thread running through every undertaking."

sentences.zh: 執一術而百善至，百邪去，天下順者，其唯孝乎！

translations.literal: Hold to one art and a hundred virtues arrive, a hundred evils depart, and all under Heaven is brought to accord — is this not filial piety alone!"
translations.idiomatic: Grasp this single practice and every virtue follows, every vice falls away, and the world comes into harmony — what could it be but filial piety!"

sentences.zh: 」然則孝之為德至矣，其為道遠矣，其化人深矣。

translations.literal: " Thus as a virtue filial piety is utmost; as a Way it is far-reaching; in transforming people it is profound.
translations.idiomatic: Filial piety, then, is the highest of virtues, the farthest-reaching of ways, and the deepest in its power to transform human hearts.

sentences.zh: 故聖帝明王行之于四海，則與天地合其德，與日月齊其明。

translations.literal: Therefore when sage emperors and enlightened kings practice it throughout the four seas, they unite their virtue with Heaven and Earth and match their brilliance to sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: When sage emperors and enlightened kings put it into practice across the realm, their virtue joins that of Heaven and Earth, their radiance equals that of sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 諸侯卿大夫行之于國家，則永保其宗社，長守其祿位。

translations.literal: When feudal lords, ministers, and grand masters practice it within their states, they forever preserve their ancestral altars and long hold their stipends and offices.
translations.idiomatic: When feudal lords, ministers, and grand masters practice it within their domains, they secure their ancestral altars in perpetuity and keep their rank and emoluments for generations.

sentences.zh: 匹夫匹婦行之于閭閻，則播微烈于當年，揚休名於千載。

translations.literal: When common men and women practice it in their lanes and wards, they spread a slight renown in their own day and raise a fine name for a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: When ordinary men and women practice it in village and lane, they leave a modest mark in their own lifetime and win a noble name that shines a thousand years hence.

sentences.zh: 此皆資純至以感物，故聖哲之所重。

translations.literal: All these rely on pure sincerity to move things; therefore the sage and wise hold it in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: All draw on utter sincerity to move others, which is why sages and wise men have always prized it.

sentences.zh: 田翼、郎方貴等，闕稽古之學，無俊偉之才，並能任其自然，情無矯飾。

translations.literal: Tian Yi, Lang Fanggui, and the like lacked learning in antiquity and had no outstanding talent, yet all could follow their natural feelings without forced display.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Tian Yi and Lang Fanggui had no training in classical learning and no towering gifts, yet each could follow his inborn nature without artifice or pretense.

sentences.zh: 篤於天性，勤其四體，竭股肱之力，盡愛敬之心，自足膝下之歡，忘懷軒冕之貴。

translations.literal: Deep in innate feeling, diligent in the four limbs, exhausting the strength of arms and legs, fulfilling every thought of love and respect, content with joy at their parents' knees, forgetting the honor of cap and carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply rooted in natural affection, they toiled with hands and feet, poured out every ounce of strength, and gave their whole hearts in love and reverence — finding full contentment in their parents' presence and never giving a thought to rank and emolument.

sentences.zh: 不言之化，人神通感。

translations.literal: Transformation without words — men and spirits alike were moved in response.
translations.idiomatic: Their wordless influence moved both men and spirits alike.

sentences.zh: 雖或位登臺輔，爵列王侯，祿積萬鐘，馬逾千駟，死之日，曾不得與斯人之徒隸齒。

translations.literal: Though some might rise to the rank of chief minister, be ennobled as king or marquis, amass stipends of ten thousand piculs, and keep horses beyond a thousand teams, on the day of their death they could not even be ranked with the servants of such men.
translations.idiomatic: Even those who reached the highest offices, held princely titles, piled up stipends by the ten thousand piculs, and kept stables of more than a thousand horses — on the day they died they were not fit to be counted among the attendants of such men.

sentences.zh: 孝之大也，不其然乎！

translations.literal: How great is filial piety — is it not truly so!
translations.idiomatic: How vast is the power of filial piety — is it not exactly so!

sentences.zh: 故述其所行，為《孝義傳》。

translations.literal: Therefore I relate their conduct in the "Biographies of Filial Piety and Righteous Conduct."
translations.idiomatic: I have therefore set down their deeds in the "Biographies of Filial Piety and Righteous Conduct."

sentences.zh: ○陸彥師

translations.literal: ○ Lu Yanshi
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yanshi

sentences.zh: 陸彥師，字雲房，魏郡臨漳人。

translations.literal: Lu Yanshi, styled Yunfang, was a native of Linzhang in Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yanshi, styled Yunfang, was a native of Linzhang in Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖希道，魏定州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xidao was governor of Dingzhou under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xidao had been governor of Dingzhou under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父子彰，中書監。

translations.literal: His father Zizhang was Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zizhang had served as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 彥師少有行檢，為邦族所稱。

translations.literal: Yanshi from youth had proper conduct and was praised by his clan and neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yanshi conducted himself with propriety and was praised throughout his clan and neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 長而好學，解屬文。

translations.literal: When grown he loved learning and was skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured he took to learning and became adept at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 魏襄城王元旭引為參軍事。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiangcheng of Wei, Yuan Xu, brought him in as a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xu, Prince of Xiangcheng under Wei, took him on as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 以父艱去職，哀毀殆不勝喪。

translations.literal: On his father's death he left office; his grief and emaciation nearly overwhelmed the mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he left office; his grief was so extreme that he nearly perished in mourning.

sentences.zh: 與兄卬廬于墓次，負土成墳。

translations.literal: With his elder brother Ang he dwelt in a hut by the grave and carried earth to build the mound.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Ang lived in a mourning hut beside the tomb, carrying earth by hand to raise the burial mound.

sentences.zh: 公卿重之，多就墓側存問，晦朔之際，車馬不絕。

translations.literal: The high officials esteemed him; many came to the grave to inquire after him, and at the new and full moon carriages and horses never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: High officials held him in esteem; many came to the graveside to pay their respects, and on the first and fifteenth of each month the stream of carriages never stopped.

sentences.zh: 齊文宣聞而嘉歎，旌表其閭，號其所住為孝終裡。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan of Qi heard and praised him, marked out his lane with an honorific tablet, and named his dwelling-place Filial Mourning Lane.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenxuan of Qi heard of this he expressed his admiration, erected an honorific marker at his lane, and named his neighborhood Filial Mourning Lane.

sentences.zh: 中書令河間邢邵表薦之，未報，彭城王浟為司州牧，召補主簿。

translations.literal: Xing Shao of Hejian, Director of the Secretariat, submitted a memorial recommending him, but before a reply came the Prince of Pengcheng, Chou, as governor of Sizhou, summoned him to fill the post of chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Shao of Hejian, Director of the Secretariat, recommended him by memorial, but before any response arrived Chou, Prince of Pengcheng and governor of Sizhou, summoned him to serve as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 後曆中外府東閣祭酒。

translations.literal: Later he served in succession as Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion in the central and outer offices.
translations.idiomatic: He later held the post of Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion in both the central and outer administrations.

sentences.zh: 兄卬當襲父始平侯，以彥師昆弟中最幼，表讓封焉。

translations.literal: His brother Ang was to inherit their father's marquisate of Shiping; because Yanshi was the youngest among the brothers, Ang submitted a memorial offering him the fief.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Ang was due to inherit their father's marquisate of Shiping; because Yanshi was the youngest brother, Ang petitioned to yield the fief to him.

sentences.zh: 彥師固辭而止。

translations.literal: Yanshi firmly declined and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshi firmly refused, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 時稱友悌孝義，總萃一門。

translations.literal: At the time they were praised for brotherly affection and filial righteousness, all gathered in one household.
translations.idiomatic: The age praised their brotherly devotion and filial righteousness, virtues that seemed to concentrate in a single family.

sentences.zh: 遷中書舍人，尋轉通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant of the Secretariat, and soon transferred to Gentleman of the Palace in Regular Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant of the Secretariat and soon after transferred to Gentleman of the Palace in Regular Attendance.

sentences.zh: 每陳使至，必令高選主客，彥師所接對者，前後六輩。

translations.literal: Whenever Chen envoys arrived, the highest-ranking hosts were always chosen; those Yanshi received numbered six missions in all.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever envoys from Chen arrived, the court always selected the most distinguished men to receive them — Yanshi handled such duties for six missions in succession.

sentences.zh: 曆中書黃門侍郎，以不阿宦者，遇讒，出為中山太守，有惠政。

translations.literal: He served as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate at the Secretariat; because he would not flatter eunuchs he met with slander and was sent out as governor of Zhongshan, where he had benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate at the Secretariat; because he refused to curry favor with eunuchs he was slandered and sent out as governor of Zhongshan, where his rule was marked by kindness.

sentences.zh: 數年，徵為吏部郎中。

translations.literal: After several years he was summoned as Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he was recalled to serve as Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 周武平齊，授載師下大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace for Carriage Masters.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace for Carriage Masters.

sentences.zh: 宣帝時，轉少納言，賜爵臨水縣男，奉使幽、薊。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xuan he was transferred to Junior Remonstrator, enfeoffed as Baron of Linshui county, and sent on mission to You and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan he became Junior Remonstrator, was enfeoffed as Baron of Linshui county, and was dispatched on a mission to You and Ji.

sentences.zh: 俄而高祖為丞相，彥師遇疾，請假還鄴。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Gaozu became Chancellor; Yanshi fell ill and asked leave to return to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Gaozu became Chancellor; Yanshi fell ill and requested leave to return to Ye.

sentences.zh: 尉迥將為亂，彥師微知之，遂委妻子，潛歸長安。

translations.literal: Wei Jiong was about to rebel; Yanshi had a slight foreknowledge of it, so he left wife and children and secretly returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Jiong was preparing to rebel, Yanshi had some inkling of it; he abandoned wife and children and stole back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉之，授內史下大夫，拜上儀同。

translations.literal: Gaozu commended him, appointed him Grand Master of the Palace in the Secretariat, and bestowed the rank of Senior Yitong.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu praised him, appointed him Grand Master of the Palace in the Secretariat, and granted him the rank of Senior Yitong.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，拜尚書左丞，進爵為子。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, he was appointed Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat and advanced in rank to Viscount.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne he was appointed Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat and raised in rank to Viscount.

sentences.zh: 彥師素多病，未幾，以務劇疾動，乞解所職，有詔聽以本官就第。

translations.literal: Yanshi had long been prone to illness; before long, because the duties were heavy his illness worsened, and he begged to be released from office; an edict permitted him to keep his title and retire to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshi had long been in poor health; before long the strain of office aggravated his illness, and he petitioned to resign; an edict allowed him to retain his title and retire home.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，轉吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 隋承周制，官無清濁，彥師在職，凡所任人，頗甄別於士庶，論者美之。

translations.literal: Sui followed Zhou institutions, and offices had no distinction of pure and impure rank; while Yanshi held office, everyone he appointed was carefully distinguished between gentry and commoners, and commentators praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui followed Zhou institutions, in which offices carried no distinction of pure versus impure rank; in office Yanshi carefully distinguished gentry from commoners in every appointment he made, and commentators praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 後復以病出為汾州刺史，卒官。

translations.literal: Later, again because of illness, he was sent out as governor of Fenzhou and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Later, again on account of illness, he was sent out as governor of Fenzhou, where he died in office.

sentences.zh: ○田德懋

translations.literal: ○ Tian Demao
translations.idiomatic: Tian Demao

sentences.zh: 田德懋，觀國公仁恭之子也。

translations.literal: Tian Demao was a son of Duke of Guanguo Rengong.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Demao was a son of Rengong, Duke of Guanguo.

sentences.zh: 少以孝友著名。

translations.literal: From youth he was famed for filial piety and brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was renowned for filial devotion and brotherly affection.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，以父軍功賜爵平原郡公，授太子千牛備身。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, on account of his father's military merit he was granted the title Duke of Pingyuan commandery and appointed Attendant of the Thousand Oxen for the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Kaihuang era, on account of his father's military merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan commandery and appointed Attendant of the Thousand Oxen for the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 丁父艱，哀毀骨立，廬於墓側，負土成墳。

translations.literal: On his father's death his grief and emaciation left him skin and bone; he dwelt in a hut beside the grave and carried earth to build the mound.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died his grief wore him to skin and bone; he lived in a mourning hut beside the tomb and carried earth by hand to raise the burial mound.

sentences.zh: 上聞而嘉之，遣員外散騎侍郎元志就吊焉。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and commended him, sending Yuan Zhi, Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry in Extraordinary Service, to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he expressed his approval and sent Yuan Zhi, Attendant Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry in Extraordinary Service, to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 復降璽書曰：「皇帝謝田德懋。

translations.literal: He also issued an imperial letter saying: "The Emperor thanks Tian Demao.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent an imperial letter: "The Emperor addresses Tian Demao.

sentences.zh: 知在窮疾，哀毀過禮，倚廬墓所，負土成墳。

translations.literal: Knowing you are in extreme affliction, your grief and emaciation exceed the rites, you dwell in a hut at the grave and carry earth to build the mound."
translations.idiomatic: We know you are in deep affliction, that your grief exceeds the proper measure of mourning, that you dwell in a hut at the graveside and have built the mound with your own hands."

sentences.zh: 朕孝理天下，思弘名教，復與汝通家，情義素重，有聞孝感，嘉歎兼深。

translations.literal: I govern the realm through filial principle and wish to spread the teaching of renown; moreover our families are joined by marriage and our affection has long been deep — hearing of your filial response, my praise and sighs are alike profound.
translations.idiomatic: I govern the realm through filial principle and seek to spread moral teaching; our families are moreover joined by marriage and our bond has always been close — hearing of your filial devotion, my admiration and compassion are profound.

sentences.zh: 春日暄和，氣力何似？

translations.literal: The spring days are warm and mild — how is your strength?
translations.idiomatic: The spring days are mild — how is your strength holding up?

sentences.zh: 宜自抑割，以禮自存也。

translations.literal: You should restrain yourself and preserve yourself according to the rites."
translations.idiomatic: You should restrain your grief and preserve yourself according to the rites."

sentences.zh: 」並賜縑二百匹，米百石。

translations.literal: " He also bestowed two hundred bolts of silk and a hundred piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He also bestowed two hundred bolts of silk and a hundred piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 復下詔表其門閭。

translations.literal: He further issued an edict marking out his gate and lane.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was also issued to honor his household with a public commendation.

sentences.zh: 後曆太子舍人、義州司馬。

translations.literal: Later he served in succession as Attendant of the Crown Prince and as Administrator of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Attendant of the Crown Prince and as Administrator of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 大業中，為給事郎、尚書駕部郎，卒官。

translations.literal: During the Daye era he served as Gentleman of the Palace Gate and as Director of the Carriage Office in the Secretariat, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era he served as Gentleman of the Palace Gate and as Director of the Carriage Office in the Secretariat, and died in office.

sentences.zh: ○薛濬

translations.literal: ○ Xue Jun
translations.idiomatic: Xue Jun

sentences.zh: 薛濬，字道賾，刑部尚書、內陽公胄之從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Xue Jun, styled Daoyin, was a younger cousin of Zhou, Duke of Neiyang, Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Jun, styled Daoyin, was a younger cousin of Zhou, Duke of Neiyang, who had served as Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 父琰，周渭南太守。

translations.literal: His father Yan was governor of Weinan under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan had been governor of Weinan under Zhou.

sentences.zh: 濬少喪父，早孤，養母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Jun lost his father in youth and was orphaned early; he supported his mother and was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Jun lost his father in childhood and was orphaned young; he supported his mother and became renowned for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 幼好學，有志行，尋師于長安。

translations.literal: From childhood he loved learning, had resolve and conduct, and sought a teacher in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he loved learning and showed strength of character; he went to Chang'an in search of a teacher.

sentences.zh: 時初平江陵，何妥歸國，見而異之，授以經業。

translations.literal: At that time Jiangling had just been pacified; He Tuo returned to the state, saw him and regarded him as extraordinary, and taught him the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangling had just been pacified; He Tuo had returned from captivity, saw him and was struck by his promise, and instructed him in the classics.

sentences.zh: 周天和中，襲爵虞城侯，歷納言上士、新豐令。

translations.literal: In the Tianhe era of Zhou he inherited the marquisate of Yucheng and served in succession as Senior Clerk of the Remonstrance Bureau and as magistrate of Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianhe era of Zhou he inherited the marquisate of Yucheng and served as Senior Clerk of the Remonstrance Bureau and as magistrate of Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，擢拜尚書虞部侍郎，尋轉考功侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was promoted to Vice Director of the Parks Office in the Secretariat, and soon transferred to Vice Director of the Bureau of Evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Kaihuang he was promoted to Vice Director of the Parks Office in the Secretariat and soon transferred to Vice Director of the Bureau of Evaluations.

sentences.zh: 帝聞濬事母至孝，以其母老，賜輿服機杖，四時珍味，當時榮之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that Jun served his mother with utmost filial piety; because his mother was old, he bestowed a carriage, robes, a staff, and delicacies for all four seasons — at the time this was counted an honor.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard that Jun served his mother with utmost devotion, and because his mother was elderly, he bestowed a carriage, robes, a staff, and seasonal delicacies — an honor greatly envied at the time.

sentences.zh: 後其母疾，濬貌甚憂瘁，親故弗之識也。

translations.literal: Later when his mother fell ill, Jun's appearance was so haggard with worry that kin and friends did not recognize him.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother later fell ill, Jun grew so haggard with worry that relatives and friends scarcely recognized him.

sentences.zh: 暨丁母艱，詔鴻臚監護喪事，歸葬夏陽。

translations.literal: When his mother's death came, an edict ordered the Director of Guests to oversee the funeral; he returned to bury her at Xiayang.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, an edict ordered the Director of Guests to oversee the funeral, and he returned to bury her at Xiayang.

sentences.zh: 于時隆冬極寒，濬衰絰徒跣，冒犯霜雪，自京及鄉，五百餘里，足凍墜指，瘡血流離，朝野為之傷痛。

translations.literal: At that time it was deep winter and extreme cold; Jun wore mourning garments and went barefoot, braving frost and snow from the capital to his home district, more than five hundred li; his feet froze and toes fell off, wounds bled and ran — court and countryside alike were pained for him.
translations.idiomatic: It was the depths of winter and bitterly cold; Jun wore mourning garments and went barefoot through frost and snow from the capital to his home, more than five hundred li; his feet froze until his toes fell off, his wounds bled freely — court and countryside alike were stricken with grief for him.

sentences.zh: 州裡賵助，一無所受。

translations.literal: Condolence gifts from the district and neighborhood — he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted none of the condolence gifts offered by his district and neighbors.

sentences.zh: 尋起令視事，濬屢陳誠款，請終喪制，優詔不許。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled to resume office; Jun repeatedly stated his sincere wish to complete the full mourning term, but gracious edicts would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to resume office; Jun repeatedly petitioned in all sincerity to complete the full mourning period, but gracious edicts would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 及至京，上見其毀瘠過甚，為之改容，顧謂群臣曰：「吾見薛濬哀毀，不覺悲感傷懷。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital, the emperor saw how excessively emaciated he was, changed countenance for him, and turning to the assembled ministers said: "When I see Xue Jun's grief and emaciation, I cannot help but feel sorrow and grief in my breast."
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the capital, the emperor saw how grievously he had wasted away, and his expression changed; turning to the assembled ministers he said: "When I see Xue Jun's grief and emaciation, I cannot help but feel sorrow pierce my heart."

sentences.zh: 」嗟異久之。

translations.literal: " He sighed and marveled for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and marveled for a long while.

sentences.zh: 濬竟不勝喪，病且卒。

translations.literal: Jun in the end could not bear the mourning; he fell ill and was about to die.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Jun could not survive his grief; he fell ill and was near death.

sentences.zh: 其弟謨時為晉王府兵曹參軍事，在揚州，濬遺書與謨曰：

translations.literal: His younger brother Mo was at that time a staff officer in the Military Affairs Section of the Prince of Jin's household, in Yangzhou; Jun left a letter for Mo saying:
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Mo was then a staff officer in the Military Affairs Section of the Prince of Jin's household in Yangzhou; Jun left a letter for Mo that read:

sentences.zh: 吾以不造，幼丁艱酷，窮遊約處，屢絕簞瓢。

translations.literal: I have been ill-fated; in youth I met harsh affliction, wandered in poverty and want, and often lacked even a single basket of food.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune has never favored me; in youth I suffered bitter hardship, wandered in poverty and want, and often went without even a single meal.

sentences.zh: 晚生早孤，不聞《詩》《禮》，賴奉先人貽厥之訓，獲稟母氏聖善之規，負笈裹糧，不憚艱遠，從師就業，欲罷不能。

translations.literal: Born late and orphaned early, I did not hear the Odes and Rites; I relied on my forebears' bequeathed instruction and received my mother's sage and good teaching; bearing books on my back and provisions in my bundle, I did not shrink from hardship and distance, followed teachers to pursue learning, and could not bring myself to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Born late and orphaned young, I had no training in the Odes and Rites; I relied on the teachings my forebears left me and on my mother's wise and gentle guidance; I shouldered my books and packed my provisions, unafraid of hardship and distance, followed teachers to pursue my studies, and could not bring myself to stop.

sentences.zh: 砥行厲心，困而彌篤，服膺教義，爰至長成。

translations.literal: I honed conduct and steeled the heart; in hardship I grew only more steadfast, embraced the teaching in my breast, and so came to maturity.
translations.idiomatic: I honed my conduct and steeled my resolve; hardship only deepened my steadfastness; I held the teachings close to my heart until I came of age.

sentences.zh: 自釋耒登朝，於茲二十三年矣。

translations.literal: From laying aside the plough to entering court office, it has now been twenty-three years.
translations.idiomatic: From the time I left the fields for court service, twenty-three years have passed.

sentences.zh: 雖官非聞達，而祿喜逮親，庶保期頤，得終色養。

translations.literal: Though my office was not one of great renown, my stipend was glad to reach my kin; I hoped to secure their full span of years and fulfill my duty of supporting them to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Though my office was not one of high distinction, my stipend at least reached my kin; I hoped they would live to a ripe old age and that I might support them to the end of their days.

sentences.zh: 何圖精誠無感，禍酷薦臻，兄弟俱被奪情，苫廬靡申哀訴。

translations.literal: Who could have thought that sincerity would move nothing, that calamity and cruelty would come in succession, that both brothers would be deprived of mourning feeling, and that in the mourning hut we could not give full voice to grief!
translations.idiomatic: Who could have imagined that my utmost sincerity would move nothing, that calamity would strike in succession, that both brothers would be forced from mourning, and that in our mourning hut we could not give full voice to our grief!

sentences.zh: 是用扣心泣血，隕氣摧魂者也。

translations.literal: For this reason I beat my breast and weep blood, my breath falls and my soul is shattered.
translations.idiomatic: For this I beat my breast and weep blood; my breath fails and my soul is shattered.

sentences.zh: 既而創巨釁深，不勝荼毒，啟手啟足，幸及全歸。

translations.literal: Then the wound was great and the fault deep; I could not bear the bitter anguish; with hands and feet intact, I am fortunate to return whole.
translations.idiomatic: Then the wound grew vast and the anguish unbearable; with hands and feet whole, I am fortunate at least to return intact.

sentences.zh: 使夫死而有知，得從先人於地下矣，豈非至願哉。

translations.literal: If the dead have awareness, I shall follow my forebears in the underworld — is this not my utmost wish?
translations.idiomatic: If the dead have awareness, I shall join my forebears in the realm below — what greater wish could I have?

sentences.zh: 但念爾伶俜孤宦，遠在邊服，顧此恨恨，如何可言。

translations.literal: Yet I think of you, lonely and alone in office, far on the frontier — thinking of this fills me with boundless regret; how can it be put into words?
translations.idiomatic: Yet I think of you, alone and adrift in office on the distant frontier — at this thought my regret is beyond words.

sentences.zh: 適已有書，冀得與汝面訣，忍死待汝，已曆一旬。

translations.literal: I have just sent a letter, hoping to take leave of you face to face; I have endured death waiting for you — a full ten days have passed.
translations.idiomatic: I have just sent a letter, hoping to bid you farewell in person; I have clung to life waiting for you — ten days have already passed.

sentences.zh: 汝既未來，便成今古，緬然永別，為恨何言。

translations.literal: You have not come; past and present are sundered; this distant eternal parting — what words can express the regret?
translations.idiomatic: You have not come; what was present is now past; this distant eternal parting — what words can express my regret?

sentences.zh: 勉之哉，勉之哉！

translations.literal: Strive on! Strive on!
translations.idiomatic: Press on! Press on!

sentences.zh: 書成而絕，時年四十二。

translations.literal: When the letter was finished he died; he was forty-two years old.
translations.idiomatic: When the letter was finished he died; he was forty-two years old.

sentences.zh: 有司以聞，高祖為之屑涕，降使齎冊書弔祭曰：「皇帝諮故考功侍郎薛濬：於戲！

translations.literal: The authorities reported it; Gaozu shed tears for him and sent an envoy bearing a patent of condolence and sacrifice, saying: "The Emperor addresses the late Vice Director of Evaluations Xue Jun: Alas!"
translations.idiomatic: The authorities reported it; Gaozu wept for him and sent an envoy bearing a patent of condolence that read: "The Emperor addresses the late Vice Director of Evaluations Xue Jun: Alas!"

sentences.zh: 惟爾操履貞和，器業詳敏，允膺列宿，勤謇克彰。

translations.literal: You alone had conduct that was pure and harmonious, talent and achievement detailed and keen, truly matching the arrayed stars; diligence and integrity were fully displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Your conduct was pure and harmonious, your talent and achievement refined and keen; you truly matched the stars in their courses; diligence and integrity shone forth in you.

sentences.zh: 及遘私艱，奄從毀滅。

translations.literal: When you met private bereavement, suddenly you followed destruction.
translations.idiomatic: When you met with private bereavement, you were suddenly consumed by grief.

sentences.zh: 嘉爾誠孝，感於朕懷，奠酹有加，抑惟朝典。

translations.literal: I praise your sincere filial piety, moved in my breast; libations and offerings are increased, yet this also accords with court precedent.
translations.idiomatic: I praise your sincere filial devotion, which moves my heart; the offerings I send exceed the usual measure, yet this too accords with court precedent.

sentences.zh: 故遣使人，指申往命，魂而有靈，歆茲榮渥。

translations.literal: Therefore I send an envoy to convey this former command; if your soul has awareness, receive this honored grace.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I send an envoy to convey this charge; if your soul has awareness, receive this honored grace.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas, how mournful!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how mournful!

sentences.zh: 」濬性清儉，死之日，家無遺資。

translations.literal: " Jun's nature was pure and frugal; on the day of his death his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was by nature pure and frugal; when he died his household had nothing left behind.

sentences.zh: 濬初為童兒時，與宗中諸兒遊戲於澗濱。

translations.literal: When Jun was first a child, he played with the boys of the clan by a stream bank.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun was a boy he played with the other children of the clan beside a stream.

sentences.zh: 見一黃蛇有角及足，召群兒共視，了無見者。

translations.literal: He saw a yellow serpent with horns and feet, called the boys to look together, but none saw it at all.
translations.idiomatic: He saw a yellow serpent with horns and feet and called the other boys to look, but none of them could see it.

sentences.zh: 濬以為不祥，歸大憂悴。

translations.literal: Jun took it as ill omen and returned home in great grief and emaciation.
translations.idiomatic: Jun took this as an ill omen and returned home deeply troubled and haggard.

sentences.zh: 母逼而問之，濬以實對。

translations.literal: His mother pressed him to ask; Jun answered with the truth.
translations.idiomatic: His mother pressed him until he told her; Jun answered truthfully.

sentences.zh: 時有胡僧詣宅乞食，濬母怖而告之，僧曰：「此乃兒之吉應。

translations.literal: At that time a foreign monk came to the house to beg food; Jun's mother, in fear, told him; the monk said: "This is the boy's auspicious response."
translations.idiomatic: A foreign monk came to the house to beg food; Jun's mother, frightened, told him what had happened; the monk said: "This is an auspicious sign for your son."

sentences.zh: 且是兒也，早有名位，然壽不過六七耳。

translations.literal: Moreover this boy will early attain name and rank, yet his years will not exceed sixty or seventy."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, this boy will win fame and office early in life, yet his years will not exceed sixty or seventy."

sentences.zh: 」言終而出，忽然不見，時咸異之。

translations.literal: " When he finished speaking he went out and suddenly vanished; at the time all regarded it as strange.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished speaking he departed and suddenly vanished; everyone at the time found it extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 既而終於四十二，六七之言，於是驗矣。

translations.literal: Later he died at forty-two; the words about sixty or seventy were thus fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: He later died at forty-two, and the monk's words about sixty or seventy were thus fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 子乾福，武安郡司倉書佐。

translations.literal: His son Qianfu was a clerk in the granary office of Wu'an commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qianfu served as a clerk in the granary office of Wu'an commandery.

sentences.zh: ○王頒

translations.literal: ○ Wang Ban
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ban

sentences.zh: 王頒，字景彥，太原祁人也。

translations.literal: Wang Ban, courtesy name Jingyan, was a native of Qi in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ban, whose courtesy name was Jingyan, came from Qi in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 祖神念，梁左衛將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shennian was Left Guard General of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shennian served as Left Guard General of Liang.

sentences.zh: 父僧辯，太尉。

translations.literal: His father Sengbian was Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sengbian held the rank of Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 頒少俶儻，有文武幹局。

translations.literal: Ban in youth was bold and unrestrained, with civil and military capacity.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Ban was spirited and bold, possessing both literary and military talent.

sentences.zh: 其父平侯景，留頒質於荊州，遇元帝為周師所陷，頒因入關。

translations.literal: When his father pacified Hou Jing, he left Ban as a hostage in Jingzhou; when Emperor Yuan was overrun by Zhou forces, Ban thereupon entered the passes.
translations.idiomatic: His father subdued Hou Jing and left Ban as a hostage in Jingzhou; when Emperor Yuan was overrun by Zhou armies, Ban crossed into the Guanzhong region.

sentences.zh: 聞其父為陳武帝所殺，號慟而絕，食頃乃蘇，哭泣不絕聲，毀瘠骨立。

translations.literal: Hearing his father was killed by Emperor Wu of Chen, he wailed and fainted; after the time of a meal he revived, weeping without cease, wasting away until only bone remained.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard his father had been killed by Emperor Wu of Chen, he cried out and collapsed; after the space of a meal he revived, wept without stopping, and wasted away until only bone remained.

sentences.zh: 至服闋，常布衣蔬食，藉槁而臥。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, he constantly wore plain cloth and ate vegetables, sleeping on straw.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended, he habitually wore plain cloth and ate simple food, sleeping on straw.

sentences.zh: 周明帝嘉之，召授左侍上士，累遷漢中太守，尋拜儀同三司。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Zhou commended this, summoned him, and appointed him Left Attendant Senior Master; he was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Hanzhong and soon made Pillar of State, Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Zhou praised him, summoned him, and appointed him Left Attendant Senior Master; he was promoted to Governor of Hanzhong and soon made Pillar of State, Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，以平蠻功，加開府，封蛇丘縣公。

translations.literal: Early in the Kaihuang era, for merit in pacifying the barbarians he was granted an open office and enfeoffed as Duke of Sheqiu county.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaihuang era, for his merit in pacifying the barbarians he was granted the privilege of an open office and enfeoffed as Duke of Sheqiu county.

sentences.zh: 獻取陳之策，上覽而異之，召與相見，言畢而歔欷，上為之改容。

translations.literal: He presented a plan to take Chen; the emperor read it and regarded it as extraordinary, summoned him to meet; when speech was finished both sobbed, and the emperor's countenance changed for it.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a plan for conquering Chen; the emperor read it and was struck by it, summoned him for an audience, and when he had finished speaking both men sobbed—the emperor's expression changed entirely.

sentences.zh: 及大舉伐陳，頒自請行，率徒數百人，從韓擒先鋒夜濟。

translations.literal: When the great campaign against Chen was launched, Ban himself requested to go, leading several hundred followers to cross the river by night with Han Qin's vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When the great campaign against Chen was launched, Ban volunteered to take part, leading several hundred men to cross the Yangtze by night with Han Qin's vanguard.

sentences.zh: 力戰被傷，恐不堪復鬥，悲感嗚咽。

translations.literal: He fought fiercely and was wounded, feared he could not fight again, and sobbed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: He fought fiercely and was wounded; fearing he could not fight again, he sobbed in grief.

sentences.zh: 夜中因睡，夢有人授藥，比寤而創不痛，時人以為孝感。

translations.literal: In the night he fell asleep and dreamed someone gave him medicine; when he woke his wound no longer hurt—people at the time took it as filial piety moving Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the night he fell asleep and dreamed someone gave him medicine; when he woke his wound no longer hurt—people at the time attributed this to filial devotion moving Heaven.

sentences.zh: 及陳滅，頒密召父時士卒，得千餘人，對之涕泣。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, Ban secretly summoned more than a thousand of his father's former soldiers and wept before them.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, Ban secretly gathered more than a thousand of his father's former soldiers and wept before them.

sentences.zh: 其間壯士或問頒曰：「郎君來破陳國，滅其社稷，讎恥已雪，而悲哀不止者，將為霸先早死，不得手刃之邪？

translations.literal: Among them a stalwart asked Ban, saying: "Young master, you came to break Chen and destroy its altars of state—your revenge and shame are already cleared—yet your grief never stops. Is it because Baxian died too soon and you could not kill him with your own hand?
translations.idiomatic: Some of the stalwarts among them asked Ban: "Young master, you came to destroy Chen and extinguish its altars of state—your revenge is already fulfilled—yet your grief never ends. Is it because Baxian died too soon and you could not kill him with your own hand?

sentences.zh: 請發其丘壟，斷櫬焚骨，亦可申孝心矣。

translations.literal: Please open his tomb mound, break open the coffin, and burn his bones—that too can express your filial heart.
translations.idiomatic: Please open his tomb mound, break open the coffin, and burn his bones—that too would fulfill your filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 」頒頓顙陳謝，額盡流血，答之曰：「其為帝王，墳塋甚大，恐一宵發掘，不及其屍，更至明朝，事乃彰露，若之何？

translations.literal: " Ban repeatedly kowtowed in apology until his forehead bled, and answered: "He was an emperor; his tomb precinct is vast. I fear that digging for a single night would not reach the corpse, and if we wait until dawn the deed would be exposed—what then could we do?
translations.idiomatic: " Ban kowtowed again and again in apology until his forehead bled, and answered: "He was an emperor; his tomb precinct is vast. I fear that digging for a single night would not reach the corpse, and if we wait until dawn the deed would be exposed—what then could we do?

sentences.zh: 」諸人請具鍬鍤，一旦皆萃。

translations.literal: " The men offered to bring hoes and spades, and in one day all assembled.
translations.idiomatic: " The men offered to bring hoes and spades, and in one day all assembled.

sentences.zh: 於是夜發其陵，剖棺，見陳武帝須並不落，其本皆出自骨中。

translations.literal: Thereupon that night they opened the mausoleum and split the coffin. Chen Emperor Wu's beard had not fallen away at all—its roots still grew from the bones.
translations.idiomatic: That night they opened the mausoleum and split the coffin. Chen Emperor Wu's beard had not fallen away at all—its roots still grew from the bones.

sentences.zh: 頒遂焚骨取灰，投水而飲之。

translations.literal: Ban then burned the bones, took the ashes, mixed them in water, and drank them.
translations.idiomatic: Ban then burned the bones, took the ashes, mixed them in water, and drank them.

sentences.zh: 既而自縛，歸罪於晉王。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bound himself and surrendered to take blame before the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He then bound himself and surrendered to take blame before the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 王表其狀，高祖曰：「朕以義平陳，王頒所為，亦孝義之道也，朕何忍罪之！

translations.literal: The prince reported the circumstances. Emperor Gaozu said: "I conquered Chen in the name of righteousness. What Wang Ban did belongs to the way of filial devotion and righteousness as well—how could I bear to punish him!
translations.idiomatic: The prince reported what had happened. Emperor Gaozu said: "I conquered Chen in the name of righteousness. What Wang Ban did belongs to the way of filial devotion and righteousness as well—how could I bear to punish him!

sentences.zh: 」舍而不問。

translations.literal: " He pardoned him and took no further action.
translations.idiomatic: " He pardoned him and took no further action.

sentences.zh: 有司錄其戰功，將加柱國，賜物五千段，頒固辭曰：「臣緣國威靈，得雪怨恥，本心徇私，非是為國，所加官賞，終不敢當。

translations.literal: The authorities recorded his battle achievements and proposed to make him a Grand Pillar of State and grant him five thousand rolls of goods. Ban firmly declined, saying: "Through the state's awesome authority I was able to settle my grievance; my heart was bent on private revenge, not on serving the state. The offices and rewards you would bestow I ultimately dare not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities recorded his battle achievements and proposed to make him a Grand Pillar of State and grant him five thousand rolls of goods. Ban firmly declined: "Through the state's awesome authority I was able to settle my grievance; my heart was bent on private revenge, not on serving the state. The offices and rewards you would bestow I dare not accept.

sentences.zh: 」高祖從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 拜代州刺史，甚有惠政。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Daizhou and governed with notable benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Governor of Daizhou and governed with notable benevolence.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職。

translations.literal: He left office upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He left office upon his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 後為齊州刺史，卒官，時年五十二。

translations.literal: He later served as Governor of Qizhou and died in office at the age of fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Governor of Qizhou and died in office at the age of fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 弟頍，見《文學傳》。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yi is treated in the "Literary Writings" biography.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yi is treated in the "Literary Writings" biography.

sentences.zh: ○楊慶

translations.literal: ○ Yang Qing
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qing

sentences.zh: 楊慶，字伯悅，河間人也。

translations.literal: Yang Qing, courtesy name Boyue, was a native of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qing, whose courtesy name was Boyue, came from Hejian.

sentences.zh: 祖玄，父剛，並以至孝知名。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xuan and his father Gang were both renowned for utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xuan and his father Gang were both renowned for utmost filial piety.

sentences.zh: 慶美姿儀，性辯慧。

translations.literal: Qing had a fine appearance and a clever, eloquent nature.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was handsome in bearing and clever by nature.

sentences.zh: 年十六，齊國子博士徐遵明見而異之。

translations.literal: At sixteen the Qi erudite of the National University Xu Zunming saw him and marveled.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen the Qi erudite of the National University Xu Zunming saw him and was struck by his qualities.

sentences.zh: 及長，頗涉書記。

translations.literal: When he grew up he applied himself considerably to letters and record-keeping.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he applied himself considerably to letters and record-keeping.

sentences.zh: 年二十五，郡察孝廉，以侍養不行。

translations.literal: At twenty-five the commandery nominated him as Filial and Incorrupt, but he declined to go because he was caring for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-five the commandery nominated him as Filial and Incorrupt, but he declined to go because he was caring for his parents.

sentences.zh: 其母有疾，不解襟帶者七旬。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill he did not unfasten his collar or belt for seventy days.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill he did not unfasten his collar or belt for seventy days.

sentences.zh: 及居母憂，哀毀骨立，負土成墳。

translations.literal: During mourning for his mother he grieved until only bone remained and carried earth to build the tomb mound himself.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his mother he grieved until only bone remained and carried earth to build the tomb mound himself.

sentences.zh: 齊文宣帝表其門閭，賜帛三十匹，綿十屯，粟五十石。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan of Qi honored his household gate, granting thirty bolts of silk, ten bales of cotton, and fifty piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan of Qi honored his household gate, granting thirty bolts of silk, ten bales of cotton, and fifty piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，屢加褒賞，擢授儀同三司，版授平陽太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne he repeatedly rewarded him, promoted him to Pillar of State, Third Rank, and appointed him Governor of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne he repeatedly rewarded him, promoted him to Pillar of State, Third Rank, and appointed him Governor of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 年八十五，終於家。

translations.literal: He died at home at the age of eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: ○郭俊

translations.literal: ○ Guo Jun
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jun

sentences.zh: 郭俊，字弘乂，太原文水人也。

translations.literal: Guo Jun, courtesy name Hongyi, was a native of Wenshui in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jun, whose courtesy name was Hongyi, came from Wenshui in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 家門雍睦，七葉共居，犬豕同乳，烏鵲通巢，時人以為義感之應。

translations.literal: His clan lived in harmony—seven generations under one roof. Dogs and pigs nursed from the same mother, crows and magpies shared nests, and people of the time took this as a sign stirred by their righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His clan lived in harmony—seven generations under one roof. Dogs and pigs nursed from the same mother, crows and magpies shared nests, and people of the time took this as a sign stirred by their righteousness.

sentences.zh: 州縣上其事，上遣平昌公宇文弼詣其家勞問之。

translations.literal: The prefecture and county reported this to the court; the emperor sent Duke of Pingchang Yuwen Bi to visit their home and offer condolences and praise.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture and county reported this to the court; the emperor sent Duke of Pingchang Yuwen Bi to visit their home and offer condolences and praise.

sentences.zh: 治書御史柳彧巡省河北，表其門閭。

translations.literal: The investigating censor Liu Yu, while touring Hebei, honored their household gate.
translations.idiomatic: The investigating censor Liu Yu, while touring Hebei, honored their household gate.

sentences.zh: 漢王諒為并州總管，聞而嘉歎，賜兄弟二十餘人衣各一襲。

translations.literal: Prince of Han Yang Liang, as chief commander of Bingzhou, heard of this, sighed in admiration, and gave each of the more than twenty brothers a suit of clothing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Han Yang Liang, as chief commander of Bingzhou, heard of this, sighed in admiration, and gave each of the more than twenty brothers a suit of clothing.

sentences.zh: ○田翼

translations.literal: ○ Tian Yi
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yi

sentences.zh: 田翼，不知何許人也。

translations.literal: Tian Yi—no one knows where he came from.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yi—no one knows where he came from.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，養母以孝聞。

translations.literal: He was utterly filial by nature and was known for the way he cared for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He was utterly filial by nature and was known for the way he cared for his mother.

sentences.zh: 其後母臥疾歲餘，翼親易燥濕，母食則食，母不食則不食。

translations.literal: Later his mother lay ill for more than a year. Yi personally tended her comfort, changing bedding for dry or damp; when his mother ate he ate, when she did not eat he did not eat.
translations.idiomatic: Later his mother lay ill for more than a year. Yi personally tended her comfort, changing bedding for dry or damp; when his mother ate he ate, when she did not eat he did not eat.

sentences.zh: 母患暴痢，翼謂中毒，遂親嘗惡。

translations.literal: His mother suffered sudden dysentery. Yi feared poison and personally tasted her foul discharges.
translations.idiomatic: His mother suffered sudden dysentery. Yi feared poison and personally tasted her foul discharges.

sentences.zh: 及母終，翼一慟而絕，其妻亦不勝哀而死，鄉人厚共葬之。

translations.literal: When his mother died, Yi cried out once and collapsed. His wife too died of grief, and the villagers gave them a shared burial with full honors.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, Yi cried out once and collapsed. His wife too died of grief, and the villagers gave them a shared burial with full honors.

sentences.zh: ○紐回

translations.literal: ○ Niu Hui
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hui

sentences.zh: 紐回，字孝政，河東安邑人也。

translations.literal: Niu Hui, courtesy name Xiaozheng, was a native of Anyi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Hui, whose courtesy name was Xiaozheng, came from Anyi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，周武成中，父母喪，廬於墓側，負土成墳。

translations.literal: He was utterly filial. During the Wucheng era of Zhou, when his parents died, he lived in a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to build the mound.
translations.idiomatic: He was utterly filial. During the Wucheng era of Zhou, when his parents died, he lived in a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to build the mound.

sentences.zh: 廬前生麻一株，高丈許，圍之合拱，枝葉鬱茂，冬夏恆青。

translations.literal: Before his hut a hemp plant grew to about one zhang in height, its trunk spanning a full arm's grasp, its foliage lush—it stayed green winter and summer.
translations.idiomatic: Before his hut a hemp plant grew to about one zhang in height, its trunk spanning a full arm's grasp, its foliage lush—it stayed green winter and summer.

sentences.zh: 有烏棲其上，回舉聲哭，烏即悲鳴，時人異之。

translations.literal: A crow perched on it. When Hui cried aloud the crow at once answered with mournful cries, and people found it extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: A crow perched on it. When Hui cried aloud the crow at once answered with mournful cries, and people found it extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 周武帝表其閭，擢授甘棠令。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou honored his neighborhood and promoted him to Magistrate of Gantang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Zhou honored his neighborhood and promoted him to Magistrate of Gantang.

sentences.zh: 開皇初卒。

translations.literal: He died early in the Kaihuang era.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Kaihuang era.

sentences.zh: 子士雄，少質直孝友，喪父，復廬於墓側，負土成墳。

translations.literal: His son Shixiong was by nature simple, upright, filial, and friendly. When his father died he again lived in a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to build the mound.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shixiong was by nature simple, upright, filial, and friendly. When his father died he again lived in a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to build the mound.

sentences.zh: 其庭前有一槐樹，先甚鬱茂，及士雄居喪，樹遂枯死。

translations.literal: A locust tree before his courtyard had been very lush, but when Shixiong entered mourning it withered and died.
translations.idiomatic: A locust tree before his courtyard had been very lush, but when Shixiong entered mourning it withered and died.

sentences.zh: 服闋還宅，死樹復榮。

translations.literal: When mourning ended and he returned home, the dead tree flourished again.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended and he returned home, the dead tree flourished again.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞之，歎其父子至孝，下詔褒揚，號其所居為累德里。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu heard this he sighed at the father and son's utmost filial piety, issued an edict of praise, and named their dwelling Accumulated Virtue Lane.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu heard this he sighed at the father and son's utmost filial piety, issued an edict of praise, and named their dwelling Accumulated Virtue Lane.

sentences.zh: ○劉士俊

translations.literal: ○ Liu Shijun
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shijun

sentences.zh: 劉士俊，彭城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Shijun was a native of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shijun was from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，丁母喪，絕而復蘇者數矣。

translations.literal: He was utterly filial. During mourning for his mother he fainted and revived several times.
translations.idiomatic: He was utterly filial. During mourning for his mother he fainted and revived several times.

sentences.zh: 勺飲不入口者七日，廬於墓側，負土成墳，列植松柏。

translations.literal: For seven days he took neither spoon nor drink. He lived in a hut beside the tomb, carried earth to build the mound, and planted pines and cypresses in rows.
translations.idiomatic: For seven days he took neither spoon nor drink. He lived in a hut beside the tomb, carried earth to build the mound, and planted pines and cypresses in rows.

sentences.zh: 狐狼馴擾，為之取食。

translations.literal: Foxes and wolves grew tame and familiar, and he brought them food.
translations.idiomatic: Foxes and wolves grew tame and familiar, and he brought them food.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，表其門閭。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne he honored Shijun's household gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne he honored Shijun's household gate.

sentences.zh: ○郎方貴

translations.literal: ○ Lang Fanggui
translations.idiomatic: Lang Fanggui

sentences.zh: 郎方貴，淮南人也。

translations.literal: Lang Fanggui was a native of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Fanggui was from Huainan.

sentences.zh: 少有志尚，與從父弟雙貴同居。

translations.literal: In youth he had high aspirations and lived together with his cousin Shuanggui.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had high aspirations and lived together with his cousin Shuanggui.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，方貴嘗因出行遇雨，淮水泛長，於津所寄渡，船人怒之，撾方貴臂折。

translations.literal: During the Kaihuang era Fanggui was once caught in rain while traveling. The Huai rose in flood, and at a ferry he sought passage; the boatman in anger beat him until his arm was broken.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang era Fanggui was once caught in rain while traveling. The Huai rose in flood, and at a ferry he sought passage; the boatman in anger beat him until his arm was broken.

sentences.zh: 至家，其弟雙貴驚問所由，方貴具言之。

translations.literal: When he reached home his cousin Shuanggui asked in alarm what had happened, and Fanggui told him the whole story.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached home his cousin Shuanggui asked in alarm what had happened, and Fanggui told him the whole story.

sentences.zh: 雙貴恚恨，遂向津毆擊船人致死。

translations.literal: Shuanggui, burning with rage, went to the ferry and beat the boatman to death.
translations.idiomatic: Shuanggui, burning with rage, went to the ferry and beat the boatman to death.

sentences.zh: 守津者執送之縣官，案問其狀，以方貴為首，當死，雙貴從坐，當流。

translations.literal: The ferry guards seized them and sent them to the county magistrate. After investigating, they found Fanggui the principal offender—liable to death—and Shuanggui an accomplice—liable to banishment.
translations.idiomatic: The ferry guards seized them and sent them to the county magistrate. After investigating, they found Fanggui the principal offender—liable to death—and Shuanggui an accomplice—liable to banishment.

sentences.zh: 兄弟二人爭為首坐，縣司不能斷，送詣州。

translations.literal: The two cousins each insisted he was the principal offender. The county could not decide and sent them to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The two cousins each insisted he was the principal offender. The county could not decide and sent them to the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 兄弟各引咎，州不能定，二人爭欲赴水而死。

translations.literal: Each blamed himself; the prefecture still could not decide, and both vied to throw themselves into the water and die.
translations.idiomatic: Each blamed himself; the prefecture still could not decide, and both vied to throw themselves into the water and die.

sentences.zh: 州狀以聞，上聞而異之，特原其罪，表其門閭，賜物百段，後為州主簿。

translations.literal: The prefecture reported this to the throne. The emperor heard and was moved, specially pardoned their crimes, honored their household gate, and granted a hundred rolls of goods. Fanggui later served as chief clerk of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture reported this to the throne. The emperor heard and was moved, specially pardoned their crimes, honored their household gate, and granted a hundred rolls of goods. Fanggui later served as chief clerk of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: ○翟普林

translations.literal: ○ Zhai Pulin
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Pulin

sentences.zh: 翟普林，楚丘人也。

translations.literal: Zhai Pulin was a native of Chuqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Pulin was from Chuqiu.

sentences.zh: 性仁孝，事親以孝聞。

translations.literal: He was benevolent and filial by nature and was known for how he served his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He was benevolent and filial by nature and was known for how he served his parents.

sentences.zh: 州郡辟命，皆固辭不就，躬耕色養，鄉鄰謂為楚丘先生。

translations.literal: He firmly declined every summons from the commandery and prefecture, farmed the fields himself while keeping his parents in comfort, and his neighbors called him the Master of Chuqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined every summons from the commandery and prefecture, farmed the fields himself while keeping his parents in comfort, and his neighbors called him the Master of Chuqiu.

sentences.zh: 後父母疾，親易燥濕，不解衣者七旬。

translations.literal: Later when his parents fell ill he personally tended their comfort, changing bedding for dry or damp, and did not change his clothes for seventy days.
translations.idiomatic: Later when his parents fell ill he personally tended their comfort, changing bedding for dry or damp, and did not change his clothes for seventy days.

sentences.zh: 大業初，父母俱終，哀毀殆將滅性。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Daye era both parents died, and his grief so wasted him that he nearly destroyed himself.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Daye era both parents died, and his grief so wasted him that he nearly destroyed himself.

sentences.zh: 廬於墓側，負土為墳，盛冬不衣繒絮，唯著單縗而已。

translations.literal: He lived in a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to build the mound. In the depth of winter he wore no silk padding—only a single layer of mourning hemp.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to build the mound. In the depth of winter he wore no silk padding—only a single layer of mourning hemp.

sentences.zh: 家有一烏犬，隨其在墓，若普林哀臨，犬亦悲號，見者嗟異焉。

translations.literal: The family had a black dog that followed him to the tomb. When Pulin wept in mourning the dog mourned and howled as well, and those who saw it sighed in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: The family had a black dog that followed him to the tomb. When Pulin wept in mourning the dog mourned and howled as well, and those who saw it sighed in wonder.

sentences.zh: 有二鵲巢其廬前柏樹，每入其廬，馴狎無所驚懼。

translations.literal: There were two magpies nesting in the cypress before his hut; whenever they entered his hut they were tame and familiar and showed no alarm or fear.
translations.idiomatic: Two magpies had built a nest in the cypress before his mourning hut; whenever they came inside they were perfectly tame and showed not the slightest fear.

sentences.zh: 大業中，司隸巡察，奏其孝感，擢授孝陽令。

translations.literal: During the Daye era, a Metropolitan Inspector on circuit memorialized his filial response, and he was promoted and appointed magistrate of Xiaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye reign, a Metropolitan Inspector on circuit reported his moving filial piety to the throne, and he was appointed magistrate of Xiaoyang.

sentences.zh: ○李德饒

translations.literal: ○ Li Derao
translations.idiomatic: Li Derao

sentences.zh: 李德饒，趙郡柏人人也。

translations.literal: Li Derao was a native of Bai in Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Derao was from Bai in Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖徹，魏尚書右丞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Che had been Right Assistant Director of the Secretariat under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Che had served as Right Assistant Director of the Secretariat under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父純，開皇中為介州長史。

translations.literal: His father Chun had served as Administrator of Jiezhou in the Kaifu era.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chun had been Administrator of Jiezhou during the Kaifu reign.

sentences.zh: 德饒少聰敏好學，有至性，宗黨咸敬之。

translations.literal: Derao from youth was intelligent and fond of learning, with utmost natural disposition, and his clan and kin all respected him.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Derao was quick-witted and devoted to learning, with a nature of utmost sincerity, and his entire clan held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 弱冠為校書郎，仍直內史省，參掌文翰。

translations.literal: At his capping he became a Collator and also served directly in the Secretariat, sharing charge of literary drafts.
translations.idiomatic: At his capping he was made Collator and also served on duty in the Secretariat, helping manage official documents.

sentences.zh: 轉監察御史，糾正不避貴戚。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Investigating Censor, correcting abuses without avoiding noble kin.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Investigating Censor and pursued corrections without sparing the noble and powerful.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，遷司隸從事，每巡四方，理雪冤枉，褒揚孝悌。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye he was promoted to Retainer of the Metropolitan Governor; whenever he toured the four quarters he cleared wrongful convictions and praised filial piety and brotherly respect.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daye he was promoted to Retainer of the Metropolitan Governor; on his tours through the realm he cleared wrongful convictions and commended filial sons and dutiful brothers.

sentences.zh: 雖位秩未通，其德行為當時所重。

translations.literal: Though his rank and salary had not yet reached the highest levels, his conduct and virtue were esteemed in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Though his office had not yet risen to the highest ranks, his conduct and virtue were deeply esteemed in his day.

sentences.zh: 凡與交結，皆海內髦彥。

translations.literal: All who formed ties with him were the foremost talents within the seas.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone he befriended was among the foremost talents of the empire.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，父母寢疾，輒終日不食，十旬不解衣。

translations.literal: He was utterly filial by nature; when his parents took to their beds in illness he would go a full day without eating and for ten ten-day cycles would not change his clothes.
translations.idiomatic: He was utterly filial by nature; when his parents lay ill he would go whole days without food and for a hundred days would not change his clothes.

sentences.zh: 及丁憂，水漿不入口五日，哀慟嘔血數升。

translations.literal: When he entered mourning for his parents he took no food or drink for five days, and his grief so moved him that he vomited several sheng of blood.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered mourning for his parents he took neither food nor drink for five days, and his grief drove him to vomit several sheng of blood.

sentences.zh: 及送葬之日，會仲冬積雪，行四十餘里，單縗徒跣，號踴幾絕。

translations.literal: On the day of the burial it happened to be mid-winter with deep snow; he walked more than forty li in a single layer of mourning hemp, barefoot, wailing and stamping until he nearly perished.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the burial it was deep mid-winter snow; he walked more than forty li in a single layer of mourning hemp, barefoot, wailing and stamping until he nearly died on the road.

sentences.zh: 會葬者千餘人，莫不為之流涕。

translations.literal: Those who attended the burial numbered more than a thousand, and none failed to weep for him.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand people attended the burial, and every one of them wept.

sentences.zh: 後甘露降於庭樹，有鳩巢其廬。

translations.literal: Later sweet dew descended on the trees in his courtyard, and doves nested on his hut.
translations.idiomatic: Later sweet dew fell on the trees in his courtyard, and doves built a nest on his mourning hut.

sentences.zh: 納言楊達巡省河北，詣其廬吊慰之，因改所居村名孝敬村，裡為和順裡。

translations.literal: Nomarch Yang Da was touring Hebei on inspection; he came to the hut to offer condolences, and therefore renamed the village where he lived Filial Reverence Village and its lane Concord Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Nomarch Yang Da was inspecting Hebei; he came to the hut to offer condolences and renamed the village Filial Reverence Village and its lane Concord Lane.

sentences.zh: 後為金河長，未之官，值群盜蜂起，賊帥格謙、孫宣雅等十餘頭，聚眾於渤海。

translations.literal: Later he was made Magistrate of Jinhe but had not yet taken office when bandits rose everywhere; bandit chiefs Ge Qian, Sun Xuanya, and more than ten others gathered followers in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Magistrate of Jinhe but had not yet taken up the post when bandits swarmed everywhere; chiefs Ge Qian, Sun Xuanya, and more than a dozen others gathered their forces in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 時有敕許其歸首，謙等懼不敢降，以德饒信行有聞，遣使奏曰：「若使德饒來者，即相率歸首。

translations.literal: At that time an edict permitted them to surrender; Qian and the others were afraid and did not dare submit, but because Derao's trustworthiness and conduct were well known, they sent a memorial saying, "If you send Derao, we will all follow him in surrendering."
translations.idiomatic: An edict then allowed them to surrender, but Qian and the others were afraid and did not dare submit; because Derao's integrity was widely known, they sent a memorial saying, "If Derao comes, we will all surrender together."

sentences.zh: 」帝於是遣德饒往渤海慰諭諸賊。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon sent Derao to Bohai to comfort and instruct the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent Derao to Bohai to comfort and persuade the bandits.

sentences.zh: 行至冠氏，會他盜攻陷縣城，德饒見害。

translations.literal: When he reached Guanshi, another band of robbers attacked and seized the county seat, and Derao was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Guanshi, another band of robbers stormed and took the county seat, and Derao was killed.

sentences.zh: 其弟德佋，性重然諾。

translations.literal: His younger brother Denian was one who prized keeping his word.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Denian was a man who held his promises sacred.

sentences.zh: 大業末，為離石郡司法書佐，太守楊子崇特禮之。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era he was Legal Clerk of Lishi commandery; the Administrator Yang Zigong treated him with special ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye reign he served as Legal Clerk of Lishi commandery, and Administrator Yang Zigong treated him with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 及義兵起，子崇遇害，棄屍城下，德佋赴哭盡哀，收瘞之。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, Zigong met disaster and his corpse was cast below the walls; Denian hastened there, wept his fill, and gathered and buried him.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army rose, Zigong was killed and his body cast below the walls; Denian rushed there, wept his fill, and gathered and buried him.

sentences.zh: 至介休，詣義師，請葬子崇。

translations.literal: He went to Jiexiu and called on the righteous army, asking permission to bury Zigong.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Jiexiu, presented himself to the righteous army, and asked leave to bury Zigong properly.

sentences.zh: 大將軍嘉之，因贈子崇官，令德佋為使者，往離石禮葬子崇焉。

translations.literal: The great general commended this, and therefore enfeoffed Zigong with a posthumous office, appointing Denian as envoy to go to Lishi and conduct the ceremonial burial of Zigong.
translations.idiomatic: The great general praised this, posthumously granted Zigong an office, and appointed Denian envoy to return to Lishi and bury Zigong with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: ○華秋

translations.literal: ○ Hua Qiu
translations.idiomatic: Hua Qiu

sentences.zh: 華秋，汲郡臨河人也。

translations.literal: Hua Qiu was a native of Linhe in Ji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Qiu was from Linhe in Ji commandery.

sentences.zh: 幼喪父，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: He lost his father in childhood and was known for serving his mother with filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father in childhood and was famed for serving his mother with filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 家貧，傭賃為養。

translations.literal: The family was poor; he hired himself out as labor to support her.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor, and he hired himself out as a laborer to support her.

sentences.zh: 其母遇患，秋容貌毀悴，須鬢頓改，州裡咸嗟異之。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill, Qiu's face wasted away and his beard and whiskers suddenly changed color, and throughout the district people all sighed in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill, Qiu's face wasted away and his beard and whiskers turned grey overnight; people throughout the district marveled and sighed.

sentences.zh: 及母終之後，遂絕櫛沐，發盡禿落。

translations.literal: After his mother died he ceased combing and washing himself, and his hair fell out completely bald.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died he ceased combing and bathing, and his hair fell out until he was completely bald.

sentences.zh: 廬於墓側，負土成墳，有人欲助之者，秋輒拜而止之。

translations.literal: He lived in a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to build the mound; whenever anyone wished to help, Qiu would bow and stop him.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in a hut beside the tomb and carried earth to build the mound himself; whenever anyone offered to help, Qiu would bow and refuse.

sentences.zh: 大業初，調狐皮，郡縣大獵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye a levy for fox pelts was issued, and the commandery and county launched a great hunt.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Daye reign a levy for fox pelts was issued, and the commandery and county organized a great hunt.

sentences.zh: 有一兔，人逐之，奔入秋廬中，匿秋膝下。

translations.literal: There was one rabbit men pursued; it fled into Qiu's hut and hid beneath his knees.
translations.idiomatic: A rabbit was being chased; it fled into Qiu's hut and hid beneath his knees.

sentences.zh: 獵人至廬所，異而免之。

translations.literal: When the hunters reached the hut they regarded it as strange and spared it.
translations.idiomatic: When the hunters reached the hut they took it as a marvel and spared the rabbit.

sentences.zh: 自爾此兔常宿廬中，馴其左右。

translations.literal: From then on this rabbit often lodged in the hut, tame at his left and right.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the rabbit often lodged in the hut, tame at his side.

sentences.zh: 郡縣嘉其孝感，俱以狀聞。

translations.literal: The commandery and county praised his filial response, and all reported the matter upward.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery and county praised his moving filial piety and all reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 煬帝降使勞問，表其門閭。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang sent envoys to console him and honored his household gate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang sent envoys to console him and honored his household with an imperial marker.

sentences.zh: 後群盜起，常往來廬之左右，咸相誡曰：「勿犯孝子。

translations.literal: Later when bandits rose they often passed to and fro near the hut, and all warned one another, saying, "Do not harm the filial son."
translations.idiomatic: Later when bandits rose they often passed near the hut, and all warned one another: "Do not harm the filial son."

sentences.zh: 」鄉人賴秋而全者甚眾。

translations.literal: Many in the village owed their safety to Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: A great many in the village owed their safety to Qiu.

sentences.zh: ○徐孝肅

translations.literal: ○ Xu Xiaosu
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xiaosu

sentences.zh: 徐孝肅，汲郡人也。

translations.literal: Xu Xiaosu was a native of Ji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xiaosu was from Ji commandery.

sentences.zh: 宗族數千家，多以豪侈相尚，唯孝肅性儉約，事親以孝聞。

translations.literal: His clan numbered thousands of households, most of whom vied in luxury and extravagance; only Xiaosu was frugal by nature and was known for serving his kin with filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His clan numbered thousands of households, most of whom competed in luxury; only Xiaosu was frugal by nature and famed for serving his kin with filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 雖在幼齒，宗黨間每有爭訟，皆至孝肅所平論之，為孝肅所短者，無不引咎而退。

translations.literal: Even while still a child, whenever disputes arose within the clan they all came to Xiaosu for judgment; whoever was faulted by Xiaosu invariably acknowledged the blame and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child, whenever disputes arose within the clan everyone came to Xiaosu for judgment; whoever was found at fault by Xiaosu invariably admitted blame and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 孝肅早孤，不識父，及長，問其母父狀，因求畫工，圖其形像，構廟置之而定省焉，朔望享祭。

translations.literal: Xiaosu was orphaned early and never knew his father; when he grew up he asked his mother what his father had been like, then sought a painter, had his likeness drawn, built a shrine and placed it there for morning and evening attendance, offering sacrifice at the new and full moon.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosu was orphaned early and never knew his father; when he grew up he asked his mother what his father had been like, engaged a painter to draw his likeness, built a shrine and placed the portrait there for morning and evening attendance, and offered sacrifice at the new and full moon.

sentences.zh: 養母至孝，數十年，家人未見其有忿恚之色。

translations.literal: In nurturing his mother he was utterly filial; for decades the household never saw him show an expression of anger.
translations.idiomatic: In caring for his mother he was utterly filial; for decades his household never once saw him show anger.

sentences.zh: 及母老疾，孝肅親易燥濕，憂悴數年，見者無不悲悼。

translations.literal: When his mother grew old and ill, Xiaosu personally tended dryness and dampness in her bedding, was wasted with care for years, and all who saw him were moved to grief.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother grew old and fell ill, Xiaosu personally tended her bedding for dryness and damp, was wasted with care for years, and all who saw him were moved to grief.

sentences.zh: 母終，孝肅茹蔬飲水，盛冬單縗，毀瘠骨立。

translations.literal: When his mother died, Xiaosu ate only vegetables and drank only water, wore a single layer of mourning hemp in the depth of winter, and his grief emaciated him until only bone remained.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, Xiaosu ate only vegetables and drank only water, wore a single layer of mourning hemp in the depth of winter, and his grief wasted him until only bone remained.

sentences.zh: 祖父母、父母墓皆負土成墳，廬於墓所四十餘載，被髮徒跣，遂以身終。

translations.literal: The tombs of grandparents and parents — he carried earth to build each mound, lived at the grave site for more than forty years, with hair unbound and barefoot, and there died at last.
translations.idiomatic: For the tombs of his grandparents and parents he carried earth to build each mound, lived at the graves for more than forty years with hair unbound and barefoot, and died there at last.

sentences.zh: 其弟德備，聰敏，通涉五經，河朔間稱為儒者。

translations.literal: His younger brother Debei was clever and widely versed in the Five Classics, and between the Yellow River and north was acclaimed as a Confucian scholar.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Debei was clever and thoroughly versed in the Five Classics; north of the Yellow River he was acclaimed as a true scholar.

sentences.zh: 德備終，子處默又廬於墓側，奕葉稱孝焉。

translations.literal: When Debei died, his son Chumo again lived in a hut beside the tomb, and generation after generation they were famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When Debei died, his son Chumo again lived in a hut beside the tomb, and generation after generation the family was famed for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：昔者弘愛敬之理，必籍王公大人，近古敦孝友之情，多茅屋之下。

translations.literal: The historian says: In former times to extend the principle of love and reverence one had to rely on kings, dukes, and great men; in recent antiquity to nurture feelings of filial piety and brotherly respect, most were beneath thatched roofs.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: In antiquity, spreading the doctrine of love and reverence depended on kings and great ministers; in the nearer past, the deepest filial piety and brotherly devotion flourished mostly under humble thatched roofs.

sentences.zh: 而彥師、道賾，或家傳纓冕，或身誓山河，遂乃負土成墳，致毀滅性。

translations.literal: Yet Yanshi and Daozhen — some with caps and coronets handed down in the family, some who swore body and soul to their land — thus carried earth to build mounds and brought their natures nearly to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Yet men such as Lu Yanshi and Xue Daozhen — one inheriting rank through generations, the other pledging himself to his sovereign as to mountains and rivers — still piled earth with their own hands until their bodies nearly broke, devotion carried to the edge of life itself.

sentences.zh: 雖乖先王之制，亦觀過以知仁矣。

translations.literal: Though this departed from the regulations of former kings, one may also observe excess to know benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Though such conduct violated the measured norms of the sage kings, through excess one may yet discern the heart of humanity.

sentences.zh: 郎貴昆弟，爭死而身全，田翼夫妻，俱喪而名立，德饒仁懷群盜，德佋義感興王，亦足稱也。

translations.literal: The Lang brothers contended for death yet kept their lives; the Tian Yi husband and wife both perished yet their names were established; Derao's benevolence embraced the mass of bandits, Denian's righteousness moved the founding king — these too are worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: The Lang cousins vied to die yet both lived; the Tian Yi couple died together yet won enduring fame; Derao's benevolence won over a host of bandits, Denian's loyalty moved the emperor who founded the dynasty — each story is praise enough.

sentences.zh: 紐回、劉俊之倫，翟林、華秋之輩，或茂草嘉樹榮枯於庭宇，或走獸翔禽馴狎於廬墓，非夫孝悌之至，通於神明者乎！

translations.literal: The sort of Niu Hui, Liu Shijun, and the like, and the company of Zhai Lin, Hua Qiu — some with lush grass and fine trees flourishing and withering in their courtyards, some with running beasts and soaring birds tame and familiar at hut and tomb — are these not cases where filial piety and brotherly respect reached utmost degree and penetrated to the spirits!
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Niu Hui and Liu Shijun, Zhai Lin and Hua Qiu — in some, fine trees and flourishing grass mirrored life and death in the courtyard; in others, wild beasts and birds grew tame beside hut and grave. Can this be anything less than filial piety and fraternal devotion raised to the utmost, touching even the realm of spirits?
